title: A merge into main is a release, and it names its bump
description:
Day-to-day work lands on the configured target branch. Reaching `main` is a separate act the user asks for, and it is a release: it must name patch, minor or major.

What is already here: .changeset/config.json pins `baseBranch: "main"` and `commit: false`; releases run through a version-packages pull request (see `chore: version packages (#6)`) and a staged npm publish (docs/adr/0053). Nothing today connects a SOBER node, or a merge, to a bump — a release can ship with no changeset and no version move, silently.

Close that: make the bump an explicit step on the way to `main`, wire it into the changeset the release pull request consumes, and write the ADR that says a merge into `main` is a release. CLAUDE.md already states the rule for agents; the ADR is the record behind it.

Acceptance: a merge into `main` cannot happen without a named bump, and the resulting version move matches the bump that was named. Tests land with the code.
